module_title: Bhakti and Sufi Movements - Philosophy, Sufi Terminology, and Contemporary Impact
introduction: At this level, we will understand the major philosophical principles of the Bhakti movement (Advaita, Vishishtadvaita, etc.) and important Sufi terminology. We will also explore how these movements contributed to social reform and the development of regional languages.

core_concepts.title: Shankaracharya's Advaitavada (Non-dualism)
core_concepts.description: In the 8th century, Shankaracharya propagated 'Advaita Vedanta' (Non-dualism), according to which the soul (Atman) and the supreme soul (Brahman) are one and the same.

core_concepts.title: Ramanujacharya's Vishishtadvaita
core_concepts.description: In the 11th century, Ramanujacharya refuted Shankaracharya's view and propounded 'Vishishtadvaita' (Qualified non-dualism), stating that the soul is a part of God but does not merge entirely into Him.

core_concepts.title: Sufi Terminology
core_concepts.description: Important terms include Pir/Murshid (Teacher/Guide), Murid (Disciple), Khanqah (Sufi hospice or dwelling place), and Ziyarat (Pilgrimage to the tombs of Sufi saints).

core_concepts.title: Suhrawardi Order
core_concepts.description: Founded by Sheikh Shihabuddin Suhrawardi. Unlike the Chishtis, Suhrawardi saints did not live a life of poverty and openly accepted State Patronage and political posts.

core_concepts.title: Development of Regional Languages
core_concepts.description: Bhakti saints preached in the languages of the common people (Marathi, Bengali, Awadhi, Maithili) instead of Sanskrit, triggering a golden age of regional literature in India.

important_entities.name: Nizamuddin Auliya
important_entities.significance: He witnessed the reigns of 7 Delhi Sultans. He famously told Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq: 'Hunuz Dilli dur ast' (Delhi is still far away).

important_entities.name: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu
important_entities.significance: He popularized Krishna Bhakti and 'Sankirtan' (congregational singing and dancing).

important_entities.name: Tulsidas
important_entities.significance: A contemporary of Akbar; he authored the epic 'Ramcharitmanas' in the Awadhi language.

important_entities.name: Amir Khusrau
important_entities.significance: Known as 'Tuti-e-Hind' (Parrot of India). He is credited with the invention of Qawwali and Khari Boli Hindi.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Because of the ancient theme of the Ramcharitmanas, students often mistakenly place Tulsidas in Ancient India. Remember, Tulsidas was a contemporary of the Mughal Emperor 'Akbar'.
Chishtis considered music (Sama) as a path to reach God and avoided politics, while Suhrawardis rejected musical gatherings and accepted wealth and royal titles.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: 'Khanqah' was the place where Sufi saints lived and ran a Langar (community kitchen/food).

exam_strategy_tips: Direct Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) are frequently asked on the meanings of Sufi terminology (e.g., Khanqah, Murid, Sama).
'Match the following' questions pairing Philosophies with their Founders (e.g., Advaita-Shankaracharya) are highly important for all competitive exams.
